sentences.text: The only point that arises for consideration is whether the acquisition proceedings initiated for acquiring the subject property, is deemed to have been lapsed or not.

2. The preliminary notification dated 18.01.1962 was issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for acquiring the land bearing Sy. No.267 measuring 3 acres 4 guntas, Sy.
No.268 measuring 2 acres 10 guntas, Sy. No.270(A)(B) measuring 2 acres 35 guntas and Sy. No.296 measuring 4 acres 25 guntas, all situated at Kasurgol Village, Honnavar Taluk, among other lands for the benefit of Karwar Port, which culminated in passing of an award dated 09.02.1966.
3.
Petitioner claims to be the owner of the subject lands under a registered Will dated 29/30.01.1993.
The name NC: 2024:KHC-D:884 of the petitioner has been mutated in the revenue records pertaining to the subject lands.
The respondent No.7 on 24.02.2005 issued a communication to the respondent No.4 stating that the subject lands are not required for the benefit of Karwar Port.

In turn, respondent N.5 corresponded to respondent No.4 for taking action for Victor Saver Rodrigues vs The Chief Secretary on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152003889/

sentences.text:
The Under Secretary to Government of Karnataka, PWD Department, on 17.05.2008 communicated with the Government,
PWD, Ports and Inland Water Transportation for taking a decision and reporting to the Government, as to whether the lands which have been acquired are to be retained or not.

On the information sought by the petitioner under the Right to Information Act, the respondent No.1 furnished information stating that the subject lands have not been utilized for the benefit of Karwar Port.

4. This writ petition is filed to declare the proceedings initiated for acquiring the subject land culminating in passing of the award, as deemed to have been lapsed, as stated under Section 24(2)
of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as Act, 2013).

sentences.text: 5. In response, the State Government had filed a statement of objections on 05.11.2014, inter alia stating that from the original records, an application was filed by wife of Piyadada Luis Fernandes for disbursing the compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:884 Therefore, the compensation having been received, the petitioner cannot claim the benefit under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

The petitioner filed re-joinder to the statement of objection filed by the State, stating that Luis is not the wife of Piyadada Fernandes, and Piyadada Fernandes died on 01.06.1994, and Piyadada Farnandes was married to one Smt.Rusai Cajetan Rodrigues on 07.04.1998, and to substantiate the same, the petitioner produced the death certificate and marriage certificate issued by the Parish Priest.
6. In light of the contention taken by the petitioner in the re-joinder, the State Government sought permission to withdraw the earlier statement of objection, and filed a fresh statement of objection,
and thereafter, the fresh statement of objection was filed.

The contention taken in the earlier statement of objection was reiterated, and no documents are produced to substantiate that the petitioner or the Piyadada Fernandes during his lifetime received compensation in pursuance of the award passed.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the material on record clearly establishes that in pursuance of the award passed, the possession of the subject land was not taken in a manner known to law, and also compensation amount has not been paid or deposited before the jurisdictional Court.

Therefore, the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 are applicable, and the acquisition proceedings initiated in respect NC: 2024:KHC-D:884 of the subject land is deemed to have been lapsed by operation of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

8. The learned AGA for the State would submit that the compensation was paid to the original owner during his lifetime, and the original owner had not made any claim against the government, and the same is substantiated by the documents annexed to the statement of objection.

Therefore, the owner of the subject land having received compensation, and the possession of the subject land having been taken, the petitioner cannot claim the benefit under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

10. The documents have been annexed to the statement of objection to substantiate that Smt.Luis Piyadada is the wife of P.L.Fernandes and compensation amount had been paid to the wife of the deceased owner.

To falsify the said documents, the petitioner produced the death certificate of the original owner which indicated that he died on 01.06.1994, and he was married to one Rusai Rodrigues on 07.04.1988, and the said documents have not been disputed by filing an affidavit or by producing any material to disbelieve the said documents, and after production of the said documents, the State Government had chosen to withdraw the earlier statement of objection, and statement of objection was filed afresh NC: 2024:KHC-D:884
reiterated the averments made in its earlier statement of objection.
No material is produced to substantiate that the compensation was paid to the original owner during his lifetime or to the petitioner after his death.

11. The Port Officer, Honnavar has issued a communication to the Director, Port and Inland Water Department, Karwar, stating that the possession of the subject land is with the owner, and the said land is not required for the benefit of the port, and recommended for re-conveying the land to the owner.
Therefore, it is established that the possession of the subject land was not taken under the impugned acquisition proceedings.

12. Learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his contention has placed on reliance, the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee,
Bangalore vs. State of Karnataka reported in AIR OnLine 2022 SC 381, wherein at paragraphs 10 and 11 it is held as follows:
"10. Applying the law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) to the facts of the case on hand, the view taken by the High Court while declaring the acquisition proceedings have lapsed under subsection (2) of section 24 of the Act, 2013, is unsustainable and is just contrary to the law laid down by this Court in the case Indore Development Authority (supra)

sentences.text: Even the same is also not disputed by Shri C. U Singh, NC: 2024:KHC-D:884 learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the original writ petitioners - original land owners.

Therefore,
the common judgment and order passed by the High Court allowing the writ petitions and declaring that the acquisition proceedings with respect to the lands in question have lapsed under subsection (2) of section 24 of the Act, 2013 cannot stand and the same deserve to be quashed and set aside.
11.

As observed hereinabove, though a number of other issues were raised on the legality of the acquisition proceedings under the Act, 1894 and though other points for consideration were raised/framed by the High Court reproduced hereinabove,
since none of the issues are adjudicated by the High Court on merits, we have no other alternative but to remand the matter to the learned Single Judge for deciding the writ petitions afresh and to adjudicate on all the other issues, other than the lapse of acquisitions under subsection (2) of section 24 of the Act, 2013.

At the cost of repetition, we observe that the High Court ought to have adjudicated on all the issues Victor Saver Rodrigues vs The Chief Secretary on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152003889/
4 raised and ought not to have decided and disposed of the writ petitions, adjudicating only on one issue which has been found to be erroneous.

sentences.text:
The Division Bench has also not applied its mind to this aspect of the matter NC: 2024:KHC-D:884 and has simply dismissed the appeals filed by the appellant herein."
13.

What is apparent from the legal principles established by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforesaid decision is that, to claim the benefit under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, the requirement is that not only the possession must not have been taken, but also compensation must not have been deposited or received by the original owner.

14. In the instant case, neither the possession is taken nor the compensation is paid to the original owners, and therefore, by operation of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, the acquisition proceedings acquiring the subject lands is deemed to have been lapsed.

15. It is declared that the notification dated 18.01.1962 issued under Section 4(1) of the Act, 1894, by the respondent No.6, culminating in passing of the award dated 05.03.1966 passed by the respondent No.6 is deemed to have lapsed by operation of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 insofar as it relates to the subject land.
16. This Court, in this order has not conferred any right of ownership in favour of the petitioner in respect of the subject land.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
